flags.water-sewer: Whether this lot has water and sewer access is unknown and hasn't been scored, so you'll need to request an availability letter from PWSA [utilities.water_sewer].
flags.adu: A proposed rule (not yet law) could allow up to 2 accessory dwelling units by right on this parcel's RM-M zoning, each no more than 1,000 sq ft and 30 ft tall, with no requirement that the owner live on site [zoning.district, reform.status]. This bill is still 'Held In Council' with a hearing planned, so it cannot be relied on yet [reform.status].
flags.parking-minimum: The same proposed bill would remove minimum off-street parking requirements, which could free up land and money for more housing, but this is not yet law [reform.status].
flags.affordable-housing-bonus: The proposed bill also includes an optional Affordable Housing Bonus, and this parcel is outside the Inclusionary Housing Overlay so that separate mandatory program doesn't apply here [overlay.iz, reform.status]. Again, this bonus is only proposed, not yet in effect [reform.status].
flags.gap-financing: This parcel is in a neighborhood with a low median land value per square foot, so projects here often need extra ('gap') financing; this is just a note, not a penalty on the score [hood.median_land_psf].
flags.phfa-infill: Because this is a vacant lot in a lower-value area, it may qualify for PHFA infill or blight-related scoring benefits, but you should confirm this against PHFA's current criteria [landuse.vacant, hood.median_land_psf].
flags.public-owner: This parcel is owned by the City, which may make it easier to acquire through a public disposition process, though this is not guaranteed [owner.type].
